statement: Two paper strips are each 10 cm long. They are glued together so that they overlap by 3 cm, making one long strip. How long is the long strip?

choices.misconception: I took the 3 cm overlap away from one strip and stopped there.
I took the 3 cm overlap away from both strips, so I got 7 + 7.
I put the strips end to end and forgot that they overlap.
I added the 3 cm overlap on instead of taking it away.

hints: Draw the two strips, one a little on top of the other.
The 3 cm where the strips overlap belongs to both strips, but it is only 3 cm of the long strip. How far does the second strip stick out past the end of the first?
The first strip gives 10 cm. The second strip sticks out past it by 10 - 3 = 7 cm.

solutions.reliable: Draw the first strip, 10 cm long. The second strip starts 3 cm before the end of the first, so only 10 - 3 = 7 cm of it sticks out past the first strip. The long strip is 10 + 7 = 17 cm. The idea to keep: a quick drawing shows that an overlap is counted once, not twice.
solutions.elegant: End to end the strips would make 10 + 10 = 20 cm. The overlap hides 3 cm of that, so the long strip is 20 - 3 = 17 cm. The idea to keep: count everything, then take away the part that is counted twice.

whyOnTest: Drawing the diagram makes the overlap visible, and each wrong choice comes from taking the overlap away the wrong number of times.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
